learning_outcomes.text: Know the evolution of production machines towards automated systems.
Use computer-based planning and manufacturing assistance tools.
Work in a robotic manufacturing environment.
Develop tooling suitable for the level of process automation.

syllabus_topics: Evolution of manufacturing machines and systems
Grippers and tools used in industrial robots
Design for Assembly (DFA): manipulation, insertion, fastening
Design for Manufacturing (DFM): process and material selection
Examples of manufacturing-oriented design: machining, plastic injection, sheet metal forming
assessment_rules: The final grade for the general evaluation model is calculated as (0.70 x Theoretical-practical knowledge) + (0.20 x Laboratory practical knowledge) + (0.10 x Active student participation), with no minimum grade required for any component. For students opting for the differentiated evaluation model, the final grade is calculated as (0.75 x Theoretical-practical knowledge) + (0.25 x Laboratory practical knowledge) through a single written exam. Both evaluation systems are applicable to all ordinary and extraordinary calls. In case of doubt regarding authorship or unauthorized means, a face-to-face defense may be requested.
